❯ Run the shell command sleep 6, then without more tools write about 400 words
  on the history of the bicycle as plain paragraphs.

  Ran 1 shell command

❯ Queued note: after that, add one line about kites.

⏺ The bicycle developed over about two hundred years, from a simple wooden
  machine with no pedals to the light, geared frames used today. The first known
  version was the draisine, built by Karl Drais in Germany in 1817. It had two
  wheels in a line and no pedals. The rider pushed the machine along the ground
  with his feet.

  In the 1860s, French builders added pedals to the front wheel. These machines
  were called velocipedes. Riders called them "boneshakers" because their iron
  tires gave a hard ride on stone roads. The front wheel was large, so the
  machine was fast. It was also hard to steer and dangerous to ride.

  The high-wheel bicycle, known as the penny-farthing, followed in the 1870s.
  Its front wheel grew to about five feet across. The rider sat high above the
  road. A fall from that height could cause serious injury. Few people rode
  these machines for long. The design did show that a larger wheel covered more
  distance with each turn of the pedals.

  In 1885, John Kemp Starley built the Rover safety bicycle in England. It had
  two wheels of equal size. A chain drove the rear wheel. The rider sat low and
  could reach the ground easily. This layout is the basis of the modern bicycle.

  Pneumatic tires arrived in 1888. John Boyd Dunlop, a Scottish veterinarian,
  made an air-filled tire for his son's tricycle. The air-filled tire gave a
  much softer ride than solid rubber. Cycling became popular with women,
  workers, and young people. It gave people a way to travel farther than walking
  allowed.

  Later changes included the freewheel, multiple gears, and lighter frames made
  of steel, then aluminum, then carbon fiber. Today, bicycles serve sport,
  commuting, and delivery work. Millions of people in cities ride them every
  day.

  Kites were flown in China more than 2,000 years ago, long before the bicycle
  existed.
